literal: Hulü Jin; son Guang; Xian
idiomatic: Hulü Jin; son Guang; Xian

literal: Hulü Jin, styled Aluodun, was a native of the Chile tribe in Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin, styled Aluodun, was a native of the Chile tribe in Shuozhou.

literal: His great-great-grandfather Beihouli, renowned beyond the frontier for strength and bravery, led his household to submit in the reign of Emperor Daowu of Wei and was granted the title Duke of Mengdu.
idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather Beihouli, renowned beyond the frontier for strength and bravery, led his household to submit in the reign of Emperor Daowu of Wei and was granted the title duke of Mengdu.

literal: His grandfather Fandijin served as Director of the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: His grandfather Fandijin served as director of the palace secretariat.

literal: His father Dana'gui served as Director of Splendid Honors and First Chief of the Submitted Tribes.
idiomatic: His father Dana'gui served as director of splendid honors and first chief of the submitted tribes.

literal: During Tianping, when Jin rose high, Dana'gui was posthumously made Duke of Works.
idiomatic: During Tianping, when Hulü Jin rose high, his father Dana'gui was posthumously made duke of works.

literal: Jin was honest and straightforward by nature, skilled at riding and archery; in campaigning he used Xiongnu methods — reading dust to know how many horse and foot were on the march, sniffing the ground to gauge an army's distance.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin was honest and straightforward by nature, skilled at riding and archery; in campaigning he used Xiongnu methods — reading dust to know how many horse and foot were on the march, sniffing the ground to gauge an army's distance.

literal: At first he served as a military commander; with the garrison general of Huaishuo, Yang Jun, he escorted the Ruru ruler Anagui back north.
idiomatic: At first he served as a military commander; with the garrison general of Huaishuo, Yang Jun, he escorted the Ruru ruler Anagui back north.

literal: Anagui watched Jin hunting with bow and arrow and sighed deeply at his skill.
idiomatic: Anagui watched Hulü Jin hunting with bow and arrow and sighed deeply at his skill.

literal: Later Anagui raided Gaolu; Jin resisted and defeated him.
idiomatic: Later Anagui raided Gaolu; Hulü Jin resisted and defeated him.

literal: At the end of Zhenguang, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Jin gathered troops and submitted to him, and Baling made Jin a nominal king.
idiomatic: At the end of Zhenguang, Poliuhan Baling raised rebellion; Hulü Jin gathered troops and submitted to him, and Baling made Jin a nominal king.

literal: Jin judged that Baling would ultimately be destroyed and annihilated; he then led the ten thousand households under his command to Yunzhou to surrender and was at once appointed Second Chief of the Submitted Tribes.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin judged that Baling would ultimately be destroyed and annihilated; he then led the ten thousand households under his command to Yunzhou to surrender and was at once appointed second chief of the submitted tribes.

literal: He gradually led his force south out of Huangguadui but was defeated by Du Luozhou; his troops scattered, and Jin and his elder brother Ping alone escaped to Erzhu Rong.
idiomatic: He gradually led his force south out of Huangguadui but was defeated by Du Luozhou; his troops scattered, and Hulü Jin and his elder brother Ping alone escaped to Erzhu Rong.

literal: Rong memorialized to have Jin made a separate commander; he rose in succession to grand commander.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong memorialized to have Hulü Jin made a separate commander; he rose in succession to grand commander.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Jin was granted the title Baron of Fucheng County and additionally made General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel of the Towered Cavalry.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang ascended the throne, Hulü Jin was granted the title baron of Fucheng County and additionally made general who pacifies the north and colonel of the towered cavalry.

literal: He followed in the defeats of Ge Rong and Yuan Hao, earned repeated battle merit, and was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: He followed in the defeats of Ge Rong and Yuan Hao, earned repeated battle merit, and was promoted to grand general who pacifies the south.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao and others rose in rebellion, the Grand Ancestor secretly harbored a plan to restore the realm; Jin, together with Lou Zhao, Kudie Gan, and others, approved the great design and then followed in raising the righteous banner.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao and others rose in rebellion, Gao Huan secretly harbored a plan to restore the realm; Hulü Jin, together with Lou Zhao, Kudie Gan, and others, approved the great design and then followed in raising the righteous banner.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor attacked Ye from the south, he left Jin to hold Xindu, made him Grand Commander of the six provinces of Heng, Yun, Yan, Shuo, Xian, and Yu, and entrusted him with rear affairs; separately Jin attacked Li Xiu and defeated him, and was promoted to Right Director of Splendid Honors.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan attacked Ye from the south, he left Hulü Jin to hold Xindu, made him grand commander of the six provinces of Heng, Yun, Yan, Shuo, Xian, and Yu, and entrusted him with rear affairs; separately Jin attacked Li Xiu and defeated him, and was promoted to right director of splendid honors.

literal: He joined the Grand Ancestor at Ye and then followed in pacifying Jinyang and pursuing the destruction of Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: He joined Gao Huan at Ye and then followed in pacifying Jinyang and pursuing the destruction of Erzhu Zhao.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang, Jin was made Governor of Fen Province and Grand Commander of that province, and his rank was advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang, Hulü Jin was made governor of Fen Province and grand commander of that province, and his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Hediouling west of the river.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in defeating Hediouling west of the river.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he moved to Ye; Jin was ordered to lead thirty thousand foot and horse to garrison Fengling against Western raiders; when the campaign ended, he returned to Jinyang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, he moved to Ye; Hulü Jin was ordered to lead thirty thousand foot and horse to garrison Fengling against Western raiders; when the campaign ended, he returned to Jinyang.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in battle at Shayuan; the army withdrew without success, and for this the cities of eastern Yong were again seized by the Western army; Jin was dispatched with Wei Jing, Kudie Gan, and others to recover them.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in battle at Shayuan; the army withdrew without success, and for this the cities of eastern Yong were again seized by the Western army; Hulü Jin was dispatched with Wei Jing, Kudie Gan, and others to recover them.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era, the Zhou Emperor Wen again launched a great campaign toward Heyang.
idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era, Yuwen Tai again launched a great campaign toward Heyang.

literal: The Grand Ancestor led troops to attack him and sent Jin straight to Tai Province to form pincers.
idiomatic: Gao Huan led troops to attack him and sent Hulü Jin straight to Tai Province to form pincers.

literal: When Jin reached Jin Province, because the army had withdrawn he did not advance; he then joined the mobile headquarters commander Xue Xiuyi in besieging the bandits at Qiaoshan.
idiomatic: When Hulü Jin reached Jin Province, because the army had withdrawn he did not advance; he then joined the mobile headquarters commander Xue Xiuyi in besieging the bandits at Qiaoshan.

literal: Before long the Grand Ancestor arrived; together they pacified the enemy, and Jin then followed the Grand Ancestor in capturing several cities including Southern Jiang and Shao Commandery.
idiomatic: Before long Gao Huan arrived; together they pacified the enemy, and Hulü Jin then followed Gao Huan in capturing several cities including Southern Jiang and Shao Commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi, Governor of Northern Yu Province, held the west of the city and rebelled, and the Zhou Emperor Wen invaded Luoyang.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuding, Gao Zhongmi, governor of Northern Yu Province, held the west of the city and rebelled, and Yuwen Tai invaded Luoyang.

literal: The Grand Ancestor had Jin command Liu Feng, Bu Dahan Sa, and others with several tens of thousands of foot and horse to hold Heyang city against him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan had Hulü Jin command Liu Feng, Bu Dahan Sa, and others with several tens of thousands of foot and horse to hold Heyang city against him.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor arrived, Jin again followed in defeating Zhongmi.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan arrived, Hulü Jin again followed in defeating Zhongmi.

literal: When the army returned, he was made Grand Marshal, his title was changed to Duke of Shicheng Commandery with a fief of one thousand households, and he was transferred to First Chief of the Submitted Tribes.
idiomatic: When the army returned, he was made grand marshal, his title was changed to duke of Shicheng Commandery with a fief of one thousand households, and he was transferred to first chief of the submitted tribes.

literal: In the third year, the Grand Ancestor led troops on a surprise attack against the Mountain Hu, dividing into two routes.
idiomatic: In the third year, Gao Huan led troops on a surprise attack against the Mountain Hu, dividing into two routes.

literal: Jin was made army supervisor of the southern route and went out by Huanglu Ridge.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin was made army supervisor of the southern route and went out by Huanglu Ridge.

literal: The Grand Ancestor himself went by the northern route, crossed Chihong Ridge, joined Jin at Wutu Fort, and together they attacked and defeated the enemy.
idiomatic: Gao Huan himself went by the northern route, crossed Chihong Ridge, joined Hulü Jin at Wutu Fort, and together they attacked and defeated the enemy.

literal: When the army returned, he went out as Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: When the army returned, he went out as governor of Ji Province.

literal: In the fourth year, an edict ordered Jin to lead troops by the Wusu route to join the Grand Ancestor at Jin Province, and he then followed in the attack on Yubi.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, an edict ordered Hulü Jin to lead troops by the Wusu route to join Gao Huan at Jin Province, and he then followed in the attack on Yubi.

literal: When the army returned, the Grand Ancestor had Jin command the whole host on the return to Jinyang.
idiomatic: When the army returned, Gao Huan had Hulü Jin command the whole host on the return to Jinyang.

literal: When Shizong succeeded to affairs, Hou Jing held Yingchuan and surrendered to Western Wei; an edict dispatched Jin to command Pan Le, Xue Guyuan, and others to hold Heyang in defense.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to affairs, Hou Jing held Yingchuan and surrendered to Western Wei; an edict dispatched Hulü Jin to command Pan Le, Xue Guyuan, and others to hold Heyang in defense.

literal: Western Wei sent its Grand Commander Li Jinghe and Jogan Bao leading several tens of thousands of horse and foot, intending to go from Xincheng to relieve Hou Jing.
idiomatic: Western Wei sent its grand commander Li Jinghe and Jogan Bao leading several tens of thousands of horse and foot, intending to go from Xincheng to relieve Hou Jing.

literal: Jin led troops and halted at Guangwu to intercept them; Jinghe and the others, hearing of it, withdrew and fled.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin led troops and halted at Guangwu to intercept them; Jinghe and the others, hearing of it, withdrew and fled.

literal: He returned as Governor of Si Province and again led his division to build the three forts of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan at Yiyang, posting garrisons before returning.
idiomatic: He returned as governor of Si Province and again led his division to build the three forts of Yangzhi, Baijia, and Huyan at Yiyang, posting garrisons before returning.

literal: When Hou Jing fled to Southern Yu, Western Wei Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators Wang Sizheng entered and seized Yingchuan.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing fled to Southern Yu, Western Wei commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators Wang Sizheng entered and seized Yingchuan.

literal: Shizong dispatched Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others to lead troops and besiege the city.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng dispatched Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, Liu Feng, and others to lead troops and besiege the city.

literal: An edict again ordered Jin to supervise Peng Le, Kezhuhun Daoyuan, and others in going out to encamp at Heyang and cut off their route of rescue.
idiomatic: An edict again ordered Hulü Jin to supervise Peng Le, Kezhuhun Daoyuan, and others in going out to encamp at Heyang and cut off their route of rescue.

literal: An edict again ordered Jin to lead troops to join the attack on Yingchuan.
idiomatic: An edict again ordered Hulü Jin to lead troops to join the attack on Yingchuan.

literal: When the affair was settled, Jin was again sent to lead troops from Eban to transport grain to Yiyang.
idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Hulü Jin was again sent to lead troops from Eban to transport grain to Yiyang.

literal: The Western Wei commander of Jiuchu Fort, Ma Shaolong, held a strategic pass and fought; Jin defeated him.
idiomatic: The Western Wei commander of Jiuchu Fort, Ma Shaolong, held a strategic pass and fought; Hulü Jin defeated him.

literal: For merit he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Anping County.
idiomatic: For merit he was separately enfeoffed baron of Anping County.

literal: When Xianzu received the abdication, Jin was enfeoffed Prince of Xianyang Commandery, remaining governor as before.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang received the abdication, Hulü Jin was enfeoffed prince of Xianyang Commandery, remaining governor as before.

literal: That winter he attended court at the Jinyang palace.
idiomatic: That winter he attended court at the Jinyang palace.

literal: Jin fell ill; the emperor visited his residence to look in on him, granted him medicine, and palace envoys came without cease.
idiomatic: Hulü Jin fell ill; the emperor visited his residence to look in on him, granted him medicine, and palace envoys came without cease.

literal: When his illness healed, he returned to his province.
idiomatic: When his illness healed, he returned to his province.

literal: In the third year, he was appointed Grand Preceptor at his post.
idiomatic: In the third year, he was appointed grand preceptor at his post.

literal: The emperor campaigned against Xi bandits, and Jin followed the emperor on the march.
idiomatic: The emperor campaigned against Xi bandits, and Hulü Jin followed the emperor on the march.

literal: When the army returned, the emperor visited Si Province, feasted and shot with Jin, and then departed.
idiomatic: When the army returned, the emperor visited Si Province, feasted and shot with Hulü Jin, and then departed.

literal: In the fourth year, he was relieved of his governorship and returned to Jinyang as Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was relieved of his governorship and returned to Jinyang as grand preceptor.

literal: The imperial carriage again visited his residence; the six palaces and all the princes followed; wine was set out and music performed, and only at the end of the night did the revel end.
idiomatic: The imperial carriage again visited his residence; the six palaces and all the princes followed; wine was set out and music performed, and only at the end of the night did the revel end.

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; he made Jin's second son Fengle General of Martial Guards and said to Jin, "Your Grace's founding merit aided the mandate; father and son are loyal — I shall bind us by marriage and make you a frontier shield forever.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased; he made Hulü Jin's second son Fengle general of martial guards and said to Jin, "Your Grace's founding merit aided the mandate; father and son are loyal — I shall bind us by marriage and make you a frontier shield forever.

literal: " An edict then ordered Jin's grandson Wudu to marry Princess Yining.
idiomatic: " An edict then ordered Hulü Jin's grandson Wudu to marry Princess Yining.

literal: On the day the rites were completed, the emperor followed the empress dowager in visiting Jin's residence; the empress, crown prince, and all the princes followed — such was the favor and intimacy shown him.
idiomatic: On the day the rites were completed, the emperor followed the empress dowager in visiting Hulü Jin's residence; the empress, crown prince, and all the princes followed — such was the favor and intimacy shown him.

literal: Later, because the Ruru were broken by the Turks and their clans scattered, fearing they would violate the frontier and alarm the border people, an edict ordered Jin to lead twenty thousand horsemen to encamp at Baidao in defense.
idiomatic: Later, because the Ruru were broken by the Turks and their clans scattered, fearing they would violate the frontier and alarm the border people, an edict ordered Hulü Jin to lead twenty thousand horsemen to encamp at Baidao in defense.

literal: The barbarian chieftain Doubatu Jiubei was secretly leading more than three thousand households westward; scouts returned and reported; Jin drove his division in pursuit and captured the whole host.
idiomatic: The barbarian chieftain Doubatu Jiubei was secretly leading more than three thousand households westward; scouts returned and reported; Hulü Jin drove his division in pursuit and captured the whole host.

literal: Ruru Danbo was about to move the whole nation west; Jin captured his scouts and sent them in, and also memorialized describing how the barbarians could be attacked and taken.
idiomatic: Ruru Danbo was about to move the whole nation west; Hulü Jin captured his scouts and sent them in, and also memorialized describing how the barbarians could be attacked and taken.

literal: Xianzu thereupon led troops and together with Jin attacked them at Tulai, capturing more than twenty thousand households before returning.
idiomatic: Gao Yang thereupon led troops and together with Hulü Jin attacked them at Tulai, capturing more than twenty thousand households before returning.

literal: His rank was advanced to Right Chancellor, with income from Qi Province; he was transferred to Left Chancellor.
idiomatic: His rank was advanced to right chancellor, with income from Qi Province; he was transferred to left chancellor.

literal: Guang, styled Mingyue, from youth was skilled at riding and archery and was renowned for martial prowess.
idiomatic: Guang, styled Mingyue, from youth was skilled at riding and archery and was renowned for martial prowess.

literal: At the end of Wei, he followed Jin on the western campaign; the Zhou Emperor Wen's chief administrator Mo Xiaohui was then in the ranks; Guang galloped forward and shot him, then captured him on the field — Guang was then seventeen.
idiomatic: At the end of Wei, he followed Hulü Jin on the western campaign; Yuwen Tai's chief administrator Mo Xiaohui was then in the ranks; Hulü Guang galloped forward and shot him, then captured him on the field — Guang was then seventeen.

literal: The Grand Ancestor praised this and at once promoted him to grand commander.
idiomatic: Gao Huan praised this and at once promoted Hulü Guang to grand commander.

literal: When Shizong was heir apparent, he was brought in as a trusted commander; he was gradually promoted to General Who Represses Barbarians and cumulatively advanced to General of the Guard.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was heir apparent, Hulü Guang was brought in as a trusted commander; he was gradually promoted to general who represses barbarians and cumulatively advanced to general of the guard.

literal: In the fifth year of Wuding, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Yongle County.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wuding, he was enfeoffed viscount of Yongle County.

literal: Once he followed Shizong in a hunt at Huan Bridge; he saw a great bird soaring above the clouds; Guang drew his bow and shot it, striking it square in the neck.
idiomatic: Once he followed Gao Cheng in a hunt at Huan Bridge; he saw a great bird soaring above the clouds; Hulü Guang drew his bow and shot it, striking it square in the neck.

literal: The bird was the size of a wheel; it spun downward to earth — it was a great eagle.
idiomatic: The bird was the size of a wheel; it spun downward to earth — it was a great eagle.

literal: Shizong took it to look at it and was deeply struck by the marvel.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng took it to look at it and was deeply struck by the marvel.

literal: Xing Zichao, an aide in the chancellor's office, saw it and sighed, "This is an eagle-shooter.
idiomatic: Xing Zichao, an aide in the chancellor's office, saw it and sighed, "This is an eagle-shooter.

literal: " At the time he was known by the sobriquet Commander Who Drops Eagles.
idiomatic: " At the time he was known by the sobriquet Commander Who Drops Eagles.

literal: Soon he also served as Left General of the Guard and his rank was advanced to baron.
idiomatic: Soon he also served as left general of the guard and his rank was advanced to baron.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was granted Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators and separately enfeoffed Viscount of Xi'an County.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was granted commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators and separately enfeoffed viscount of Xi'an County.

literal: In the third year of Tianbao, he followed a campaign beyond the frontier; Guang went ahead as vanguard and broke the enemy, beheading many and taking captives, and also seizing mixed livestock.
idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao, he followed a campaign beyond the frontier; Hulü Guang went ahead as vanguard and broke the enemy, beheading many and taking captives, and also seizing mixed livestock.

literal: On returning, he was made Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: On returning, he was made governor of Jin Province.

literal: To the east were the three Zhou forts of Tianzhu, Xin'an, and Niutou, which recruited fugitives and repeatedly raided and plundered.
idiomatic: To the east were the three Zhou forts of Tianzhu, Xin'an, and Niutou, which recruited fugitives and repeatedly raided and plundered.

literal: In the seventh year, Guang led five thousand foot and horse in a surprise attack and broke them; he also greatly defeated the Zhou commissioner Wang Jingjun and others, taking more than five hundred captives and more than a thousand head of mixed livestock before returning.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, Hulü Guang led five thousand foot and horse in a surprise attack and broke them; he also greatly defeated the Zhou commissioner Wang Jingjun and others, taking more than five hundred captives and more than a thousand head of mixed livestock before returning.

literal: In the ninth year, he again led troops and took the four Zhou forts of Jiangchuan, Baima, Huaijiao, and Yicheng.
idiomatic: In the ninth year, he again led troops and took the four Zhou forts of Jiangchuan, Baima, Huaijiao, and Yicheng.

literal: He was made Governor of Shuo Province.
idiomatic: He was made governor of Shuo Province.

literal: In the tenth year, he was made Special Grand Master and Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: In the tenth year, he was made special grand master and commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators.

literal: In the second month, he led ten thousand horsemen to attack the Zhou opener of a government office Cao Huigong and beheaded him.
idiomatic: In the second month, he led ten thousand horsemen to attack the Zhou opener of a government office Cao Huigong and beheaded him.

literal: The commissioner of Baigu Fort, Xue Yusheng, abandoned the city and fled; Guang then took Wenhou Fort, established a garrison, set palisades, and returned.
idiomatic: The commissioner of Baigu Fort, Xue Yusheng, abandoned the city and fled; Hulü Guang then took Wenhou Fort, established a garrison, set palisades, and returned.

literal: In the first year of Ganming, he was made Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming, he was made governor of Bing Province.

literal: In the first year of Huangjian, his rank was advanced to Duke of Julu Commandery.
idiomatic: In the first year of Huangjian, his rank was advanced to duke of Julu Commandery.

literal: At that time Prince of Yueyang Bainian was crown prince; Suzong, because Guang's family for generations had been pure and careful and he had also shown merit to the royal house, took his eldest daughter as the crown prince's consort.
idiomatic: At that time Prince of Yueyang Bainian was crown prince; Gao Zhan, because the Hulü family for generations had been pure and careful and Hulü Guang had also shown merit to the royal house, took his eldest daughter as the crown prince's consort.

literal: In the first year of Daning, he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with income from Zhongshan Commandery.
idiomatic: In the first year of Daning, he was made right vice director of the masters of writing, with income from Zhongshan Commandery.

literal: In the second year, he was made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
idiomatic: In the second year, he was made grand tutor to the crown prince.

literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Heqing, Guang led twenty thousand foot and horse to build Xunzhang Fort west of Zhiguan Pass and also built two hundred li of the Great Wall, establishing thirteen garrisons.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Heqing, Hulü Guang led twenty thousand foot and horse to build Xunzhang Fort west of Zhiguan Pass and also built two hundred li of the Great Wall, establishing thirteen garrisons.

literal: In the first month of the third year, Zhou dispatched generals Daxi Chengxing and others to raid Pingyang; an edict ordered Guang to lead thirty thousand foot and horse against them; Chengxing and the others, hearing of it, withdrew and fled.
idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, Zhou dispatched generals Daxi Chengxing and others to raid Pingyang; an edict ordered Hulü Guang to lead thirty thousand foot and horse against them; Chengxing and the others, hearing of it, withdrew and fled.

literal: Guang pursued north, entered their territory, and took more than two thousand captives before returning.
idiomatic: Hulü Guang pursued north, entered their territory, and took more than two thousand captives before returning.

literal: In the third month of that year, he was transferred to Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: In the third month of that year, he was transferred to minister over the masses.

literal: In the fourth month, he led horsemen north to attack the Turks and took more than a thousand horses.
idiomatic: In the fourth month, he led horsemen north to attack the Turks and took more than a thousand horses.

literal: That winter, the Zhou Emperor Wu dispatched his pillar of state and Grand Marshal Yuchi Tong, Duke of Qi State Yuwen Xian, and Pillar of State and Duke of Yong State Kechi Xiong and others — their host was said to number one hundred thousand — to raid Luoyang.
idiomatic: That winter, Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou dispatched his pillar of state and grand marshal Yuchi Tong, Duke of Qi State Yuwen Xian, and pillar of state and duke of Yong State Kechi Xiong and others — their host was said to number one hundred thousand — to raid Luoyang.

literal: Guang led fifty thousand horsemen in a forced march to meet and attack them; they fought at Mount Mang, and Tong and the others were utterly defeated.
idiomatic: Hulü Guang led fifty thousand horsemen in a forced march to meet and attack them; they fought at Mount Mang, and Tong and the others were utterly defeated.

literal: Guang personally shot Xiong and killed him; more than three thousand heads and captives were cut down and taken; Tong and Xian barely escaped with their lives; all their armor, weapons, and baggage were seized, and the dead were heaped into a victory mound.
idiomatic: Hulü Guang personally shot Kechi Xiong and killed him; more than three thousand heads and captives were cut down and taken; Yuchi Tong and Yuwen Xian barely escaped with their lives; all their armor, weapons, and baggage were seized, and the dead were heaped into a victory mound.

literal: Shizu visited Luoyang, assessed merit and distributed rewards, and transferred Guang to Grand Commandant; he was again enfeoffed Duke of Champion County.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan visited Luoyang, assessed merit and distributed rewards, and transferred Hulü Guang to grand commandant; he was again enfeoffed duke of Champion County.
